topic: RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) with std::lock_guard
explanation: RAII is a C++ programming idiom where resource management (such as locking a mutex) is tied to object lifetime. In this context, std::lock_guard is a class template that acquires a lock on a mutex upon construction and releases it upon destruction, ensuring exception-safe and scope-bound resource management. This pattern simplifies concurrent programming by automatically managing lock acquisition and release, preventing deadlocks and resource leaks.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of std::lock_guard to manage mutex locking in a multithreaded context. Each thread creates a lock_guard object that acquires the mutex lock upon construction, ensuring exclusive access to the shared counter during increment. When the lock_guard object goes out of scope at the end of the function, it automatically releases the lock, exemplifying RAII. This pattern guarantees exception-safe, scope-bound resource management, preventing potential deadlocks or resource leaks in concurrent programming.
